chunks: And Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said:

No servant stretches out his two hands toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah is too gracious to return them empty, until He places in them, from His bounty and mercy, whatever He wills. So when one of you makes du'a, he should not withdraw his hands until he wipes them over his head and his face.
And in another report: "over his face and chest."
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette of raising and wiping the hands after du'a in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the etiquette of du'a, emphasizing Allah’s bounty and mercy toward the servant who raises his hands in supplication. It also instructs that after supplicating, one should wipe the hands over the head and face, and in another report, over the face and chest.
